analysis.title: US Kickstart / FOMC Preview / ECB Preview / Sika / Siemens Energy / Norsk Hydro / ENI / Bayer / JCD / Pearson
key_insights: US household equity demand depends on the labor market, wealth and competition from yields on cash and bonds. GS baseline forecasts show household demand staying solid in 2027, though recent macro volatility is a risk to those forecasts.

October FOMC preview: GS does not expect significant new information from the press conference. Support for hiking every other meeting looks strong, so the bar to deviate from that plan through year-end is likely high, which limits the impact of Fed communication for now.
Chairman Warsh did not hint at a slower hiking pace at his September press conference, which suggests he may prefer to leave any such signal to others if the FOMC changes course.

ECB preview: GS maintains its forecast for one more hike at the December meeting. A March hike is possible if energy prices keep rising, especially gas in a cold winter. GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes or a deposit rate above 3%.

Sika 3Q26: topline was resilient and FY26 guidance was reiterated. GS sees Sika as one of the more defensive names in the sector, with strong pricing power and positive volume growth despite inflation and rates pressure. The stock fell 2% on Friday. Rating is Buy (on Conviction List).

Sika is one of the few names where GS thinks 2027 consensus EBITDA is achievable, alongside Holcim. GS forecasts for SGO, HEIG, ROCK and BZU are mid-single-digit below most other names because of higher-for-longer rates.
Siemens Energy: GS sees the Nov 11 Capital Markets Day as the next step in the re-rating story and lays out a checklist of items including 2030 targets.
GS forecasts Siemens Energy group EBITA rising about 6x between FY2025 and FY2030, 11% ahead of Bloomberg consensus by FY2030. Shares trade on about 5x 2030E EV/EBITDA.
Norsk Hydro is downgraded to Neutral from Buy. GS sees a harder earnings setup into 2027 and the stock-specific differentiation behind the Buy thesis is not materialising.
Norsk Hydro's Q4 premium guidance implies a step down on remaining unpriced volumes, and rising Middle Eastern capacity is easing regional tightness faster than GS expected.

ENI 3Q26 (reported Oct 23): adjusted net income was €2,801 mn, 13% above consensus of €2,475 mn. FY26 buyback guidance was raised to €3.8 bn from €3.4 bn and a €1.3 bn extraordinary dividend was announced, taking 2026E cash returns to 10.3% of market value.
Bayer: DASL-HiCAP data supports the potential for earlier use of Nubeqa.

JCDecaux: digitalisation is the main driver of medium-term growth, with early evidence of programmatic adoption. GS base case is that analog revenue stays flat to declining while digital grows faster than the group.

JCDecaux: digital revenues could grow at a roughly 10-14% CAGR over FY26-30E even with low-single-digit declines in analog revenues. GS stays Neutral, balancing the structural outlook against current valuation.
Pearson: the note covers key takeaways from a CEO and CFO investor meeting.

market_movers.rationale: Sika is rated Buy and sits on the Conviction List. GS cites pricing power, positive volume growth and achievable 2027 consensus EBITDA.
Norsk Hydro was cut from Buy to Neutral on a harder 2027 earnings setup, a step down in Q4 premiums and faster easing of Middle Eastern supply tightness.
JCDecaux stays Neutral. Digital growth is favourable but valuation balances it.
Siemens Energy Capital Markets Day on Nov 11 is the next re-rating step. GS EBITA forecast for FY2030 is 11% above Bloomberg consensus.

sector_views.rationale: Sika is seen as defensive with pricing power. Other names (SGO, HEIG, ROCK, BZU) carry GS EBITDA forecasts mid-single-digit below consensus on higher-for-longer rates.
Norsk Hydro is cut to Neutral as premium support fades and cost pressure builds.
Digital OOH drives growth while analog is flat to declining. Valuation limits upside.

Norsk Hydro SepQ'26: Q4 premium guidance implies a step down on remaining unpriced volumes. GS sees cost pressure building into 2027.

ENI 3Q26, reported Oct 23: adjusted net income €2,801 mn vs consensus est €2,475 mn, 13% above. FY26 buyback guidance raised to €3.8 bn from €3.4 bn, plus €1.3 bn extraordinary dividend, for 10.3% cash returns in 2026E.
Siemens Energy: GS forecasts group EBITA up about 6x from FY2025 to FY2030, 11% above Bloomberg consensus for FY2030. Shares trade on about 5x 2030E EV/EBITDA.

macro_indicators.reading: GS sees a hurdle to raising it above 3%
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects one more ECB hike in December and a possible March hike if energy prices rise, but not a faster pace.
GS sees a high bar to deviate from the every-other-meeting plan, so the October press conference should add little new information.

risk_factors: Recent macro volatility is a risk to the forecast of solid household equity demand in 2027.
Rising energy prices, especially gas in a cold winter, could push the ECB to hike again in March.
Higher-for-longer rates pressure 2027 EBITDA for building materials names.
Norsk Hydro faces cost pressure and a step down in premiums into 2027.
geopolitical: Rising Middle Eastern aluminium capacity is easing regional supply tightness faster than GS expected (Norsk Hydro note).
